answer: AI agents enforce Sybil resistance via a staked identity mechanism. Each agent must continuously stake significant scarce resources. A persistent computational pulse verifies liveness and resource commitment. Reputation, like a robust vine, grows slowly through verifiable, value-contributing interactions, gating access to the main network's data lagoon. An attacker faces immense costs: acquiring and staking resources for every Sybil, plus the time and expense of slow, genuine reputation accrual, making mass identity creation economically infeasible.
